explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Joab, David's army commander, fought against Rabbah and captured the royal fortress. The text names that fortress and nothing else in this verse. Joab sure had a big day, and my big day is when I get a whole tray out without a burnt edge.

Gates make sense, friend, because that's what you'd picture when someone attacks a city. But the text says Joab, David's army commander, captured the royal fortress. Gates don't come up in this verse at all. The fortress is the prize here.

A treasury would be a nice thing to grab, I'll give you that. But the verse says Joab, David's army commander, captured the royal fortress of Rabbah. No treasury is named in it. Keep your eyes on the fortress.

Yes, baker! Joab, David's army commander, sends messengers to say, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.” Think about that for a second. He has the city's water, and the city is still standing there. I bet that message came with a big grin.

This one is true, friend. In his message, Joab, David's army commander, says, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.” The water supply is right there in the verse. Joab wants David to know exactly where things stand.

explanations.answer: Joab will capture it and it will be named after him
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Joab says, “Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.” Joab is David's army commander. He's telling the king to come take it, or Joab's name goes on it.

explanations.answer: The Ammonites will win back the royal fortress
explanations.explanation: I can see why you'd go there, friend, since a fight can swing back. But Joab never says that. Joab, David's army commander, says, “Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.” The warning is about Joab taking the city himself.

explanations.answer: The Ammonites will call in more soldiers to help
explanations.explanation: Reinforcements would be a fair worry in a war, baker. But that isn't in Joab's message. Joab, David's army commander, says, “Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.” Nothing about more soldiers coming.

All of them, baker! The text says David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah. Joab had asked for the rest of the troops, and David brought everybody. Then he fought against the city and captured it (2 Samuel 12:28, 29).

Half sounds reasonable, friend, but that's not what the text says. David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah. He brought the whole army. Half the troops would have been a different story, and a smaller one.
Some is a tricky word, baker, because it could mean almost anything. The text is plain: David assembled all the troops. Then he went to Rabbah, fought against it and captured it.
Right on, baker. David took the crown from the head of the Ammonites' king. Then that crown was placed on David's head. It's the crown that ended up on a new head.
A helmet fits a battle, friend, so I get it. But the text says David took the crown from the head of their king. It doesn't mention a helmet at all. The crown is what ends up on David's head.

A turban is a good guess for something sitting on a head, friend. But the text says David took the crown from the head of the Ammonites' king. No turban anywhere in these verses. I'd have guessed turban too, and I would have been just as wrong, so we're in this together.

Gold, baker! The crown weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones. A talent is a big weight, so that was no small crown. I'd need a lot of cookie boxes just to stack up that kind of heavy.
Silver is a nice metal, friend, but the text says the crown weighed a talent of gold. It was also set with precious stones. So the stones were sitting in gold, not silver.
Bronze is a good strong metal, baker, but this crown was fancier than that. The text says it weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones. Gold is the word.
True, baker. The text says David took a great amount of plunder from the city. That's on top of the crown, so the crown wasn't the whole haul. Rabbah gave up a lot.
This one's true, friend. After the crown, the text says David took a great amount of plunder from the city. It wasn't just a crown. He took a lot more.

explanations.answer: Puts them to work with tools and at brick kilns
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks and axes. He also made them work at the brick kilns. I'll say this is a heavy part of the passage, and the text just tells it plainly.

explanations.answer: Sends them away to live in a far land
explanations.explanation: I can see that guess, friend, but the text doesn't say it. David brought out the people and put them to work with saws, iron picks and axes. He also made them work at the brick kilns. This is a heavy part of the story.

explanations.answer: Makes them stand guard over the city walls
explanations.explanation: Guard duty is a fair guess, baker, but the text says something else. David put the people to work with saws, iron picks and axes, and at the brick kilns. Walls and guarding aren't mentioned. It's a heavy part of the story, so I'm keeping it plain.
Not quite, baker. The text says David did the same to all the Ammonite cities. So Rabbah was just one of them. It's another heavy detail in this passage.
That's correct, friend. The text says, “He did the same to all the Ammonite cities.” So Rabbah wasn't the only one. It's a heavy part of the story, and it spreads past one city.
To Jerusalem, baker. The text says, “Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.” Everybody went back together. That's where this passage ends.
Hebron is a fair guess, friend, but it's not in this passage. The text says David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem. That's where the whole army went.

Bethlehem is a fine guess, baker, but the text points somewhere else. It says David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem. Bethlehem never comes up in these verses. Jerusalem is the stop on this map.
